about: First draft of the intermediate representation's vocabulary. This file is the source of truth; operation-vocabulary.md is generated from it by corpus/tools/vocabulary_check.py, which also checks it against the corpus. 'tsql' lists the T-SQL words that lower to an entry and is what the coverage check matches on. 'detect' is an optional pattern used instead of 'tsql' when counting which artefacts use an entry. 'x' is true where the hand conversion in prototype/hand-conversion exercised the entry.
rules: Every operation has one meaning, whatever source it came from. Lowering resolves the source's behaviour, using catalog types and collations, into the operation that means exactly that.
The vocabulary grows by addition only. A new source or target may add an entry and may never change what an existing one means.
A target either handles an operation or declares it unsupported, which the report shows as manual work.
Operations are typed. Where the meaning depends on operand types, there is one operation per meaning (integer_divide and decimal_divide), not one operation with hidden behaviour.
Comparison of strings always names its comparison rule (case sensitivity, trailing-space handling), taken from the source's comparison rules at lowering (for SQL Server, its collation precedence).
The query part is a logical plan in our own words: kinds of step borrowed from Spark's plan concepts, each with the source's meaning.

types.name: integer(bits, signed)
types.meaning: A whole number of 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits. Going outside the range is an error, never a wrap. SQL Server's tinyint is integer(8, unsigned): 0 to 255.

types.name: decimal(precision, scale)
types.meaning: An exact decimal number. Results of arithmetic take SQL Server's precision and scale rules.

types.name: money(precision)
types.meaning: An exact decimal with four places, precision 19 or 10, whose multiplication and division truncate to four places at every step.

types.name: float(bits)
types.meaning: A binary floating-point number of 53 or 24 bits.

types.name: date
types.meaning: A calendar date with no time and no zone.

types.name: local_timestamp(rounding)
types.meaning: A date and time with no zone. 'rounding' says how a value is stored: to 1/300 of a second (datetime), to the minute (smalldatetime), or to a number of fractional digits up to 7 (datetime2).

types.name: timestamp_with_offset(digits)
types.meaning: A date and time with its offset from UTC kept.

types.name: string(length, unit, fixed, collation)
types.meaning: Text. 'length' is the maximum, or unlimited; 'unit' is bytes or UTF-16 units, as SQL Server counts; 'fixed' means shorter values are padded with spaces; 'collation' gives the comparison rule.

types.name: collation(case_sensitive, accent_sensitive, ignore_trailing_spaces, origin)
types.meaning: How two strings compare and sort. 'origin' is explicit, column or default, which decides precedence and whether mixing two is an error.

types.name: guid
types.meaning: A 16-byte identifier that sorts and compares in SQL Server's own byte order, which is not text order.

types.name: row_set(columns)
types.meaning: A set of rows with named, typed columns: the type of a table variable, a table-valued parameter, a result set and every query step.

types.name: cursor_handle
types.meaning: A position in a set of rows being read one at a time.

types.name: unsupported_type(source_name)
types.meaning: A source type with no neutral meaning yet: sql_variant, hierarchyid, spatial types, rowversion. Anything touching a value of this type is manual.

types.name: unknown
types.meaning: A type lowering could not establish, for example when a table shape is missing. Operations on it are flagged.

node_kinds.name: artefact
node_kinds.meaning: The outer record every artefact has: identity, artefact type, tier, dependencies, original source, status. Its body is one of the kinds below, or absent for a recognised type.

node_kinds.name: procedure_body
node_kinds.meaning: Parameters, a statement list, and what it gives back: a return code, output parameters and result sets in order.

node_kinds.name: scalar_function_body
node_kinds.meaning: Parameters, a statement list and a single returned value.

node_kinds.name: table_function_body
node_kinds.meaning: Either one query (inline) or a statement list that fills a declared row set (multi-statement).

node_kinds.name: trigger_body
node_kinds.meaning: The table, the timing (after or instead of), the events, and a statement list that can read the inserted and deleted rows.

node_kinds.name: batch_script_body
node_kinds.meaning: An ordered list of batches. Variables do not survive from one batch to the next.

node_kinds.name: opaque_fragment
node_kinds.meaning: Source kept verbatim because lowering could not express it, with its position and the reason. It records what it reads and writes in scope where detectable, and is otherwise a scope barrier.

node_kinds.name: dynamic_sql_execution
node_kinds.meaning: Execution of SQL text built at run time. The expressions that build the text are lowered; the text itself is not. Always a scope barrier, always manual.

node_kinds.name: schema_change
node_kinds.meaning: A statement that creates, alters or drops a permanent object. Schema migration is out of scope, so it is recorded and manual. Temp tables are not schema changes.

node_kinds.name: external_reference
node_kinds.meaning: A reference to an object outside the catalog: another database, a linked server, a system object.

node_kinds.name: permission_change
node_kinds.meaning: A statement that grants, revokes or denies a permission, or switches security context. Recorded and manual.

annotations.name: comment
annotations.meaning: A source comment, attached to the nearest node and carried to the generated code unchanged. Untrusted text.

annotations.name: query_hint
annotations.meaning: A table hint or query option. Kept on its step and reported as not applicable on the target.

annotations.name: module_option
annotations.meaning: An option on the artefact itself: the security context it runs under, schema binding, native compilation, encryption. Reported; none changes the conversion.

annotations.name: stored_setting
annotations.meaning: The ANSI_NULLS and QUOTED_IDENTIFIER settings stored with a routine, which lowering uses to choose between operations.

annotations.name: source_position
annotations.meaning: Where a node came from in the original. Every node has one.

annotations.name: producer
annotations.meaning: Who produced a node: deterministic code, or an LLM with prompt and model version.

annotations.name: provenance
annotations.meaning: Whether a fact a node relies on was read, parsed or assumed.

operations.name: declare_parameter
operations.meaning: A typed input to an artefact, with an optional default. An output parameter also carries a value in and gives one back.

operations.name: declare_variable
operations.meaning: A typed variable, null until assigned unless given an initial value.

operations.name: declare_row_set_variable
operations.meaning: A variable holding a row set. A rollback does not undo changes to it.

operations.name: create_temp_table
operations.meaning: A table private to the session, visible to called routines, dropped when the routine that created it returns. May declare keys and constraints.

operations.name: create_global_temp_table
operations.meaning: A temp table visible to every session. Reported.

operations.name: drop_temp_table
operations.meaning: Drop a temp table before its routine ends.

operations.name: declare_label
operations.meaning: A named point in a statement list that a jump can target.

operations.name: assign
operations.meaning: Evaluate an expression and store it in a variable, converting to the variable's type. A value too long for a string variable is cut without an error.

operations.name: assign_from_rows
operations.meaning: Set variables from a query's rows: no row leaves them unchanged; several rows leave the values of the last row processed, which is undefined.

operations.name: assign_from_single_value
operations.meaning: Set a variable from a query that must return at most one value: no row gives null; more than one row is an error.

operations.name: if
operations.meaning: Run one branch when the condition is true and the other when it is false or unknown.

operations.name: while
operations.meaning: Repeat a block while the condition is true. False or unknown ends it.

operations.name: break
operations.meaning: Leave the innermost loop.

operations.name: continue
operations.meaning: Go to the next pass of the innermost loop.

operations.name: jump
operations.meaning: Go to a label.

operations.name: return
operations.meaning: End the artefact. A procedure gives back an integer code, zero if none is stated; a function gives back its value.

operations.name: call_procedure
operations.meaning: Run another procedure with arguments by name or position, receive its output parameters and optionally its return code. Its result sets go to the caller's caller.

operations.name: emit_result_set
operations.meaning: Send a query's rows to the caller as the next result set, in the query's order if it has one.

operations.name: wait
operations.meaning: Pause for a duration or until a time of day.

operations.name: try_catch
operations.meaning: Run a block; if a catchable error occurs in it, run the handler. Not catchable: messages of severity 10 or below, and an error resolving a name at the same level as the block.

operations.name: raise_error
operations.meaning: Raise an error with a number, message, severity and state. Severity 11 or above transfers to a handler.

operations.name: rethrow
operations.meaning: Inside a handler, raise the error being handled again, unchanged.

operations.name: emit_message
operations.meaning: Send text to the caller's message stream without raising an error.

operations.name: error_field
operations.meaning: Inside a handler, one field of the error being handled: number, message, severity, state, line or procedure.

operations.name: last_statement_error
operations.meaning: The error number of the statement just run, zero if it succeeded. Every statement resets it.

operations.name: set_abort_on_error
operations.meaning: Choose whether an error ends the batch and rolls back the transaction (on) or ends only the statement (off).

operations.name: begin_transaction
operations.meaning: Start a transaction, or nest one level deeper in an open one.

operations.name: commit_transaction
operations.meaning: Close one level. Only closing the outermost level makes the changes permanent.

operations.name: rollback_transaction
operations.meaning: Undo every change since the outermost level began and close all levels.

operations.name: save_point
operations.meaning: Name a point inside a transaction.

operations.name: rollback_to_save_point
operations.meaning: Undo changes made since a named point, leaving the transaction open.

operations.name: transaction_depth
operations.meaning: How many levels are open.

operations.name: transaction_state
operations.meaning: Whether a transaction is open and can still commit: 1, 0 or -1.

operations.name: set_isolation_level
operations.meaning: Choose what concurrent changes a transaction may see. Recorded; under the single-writer assumption it changes nothing.

operations.name: declare_cursor
operations.meaning: Bind a cursor to a query, with its scope, whether it sees later changes (static, keyset, dynamic, or undefined for fast-forward) and whether it can update.

operations.name: open_cursor
operations.meaning: Run the cursor's query and position before the first row.

operations.name: fetch_cursor
operations.meaning: Move to a row (next, prior, first, last, absolute, relative) and store its columns in variables.

operations.name: fetch_status
operations.meaning: Whether the last fetch found a row: 0, or -1 past the end, -2 if the row is gone.

operations.name: close_cursor
operations.meaning: Release the cursor's rows.

operations.name: deallocate_cursor
operations.meaning: Remove the cursor.

operations.name: write_current_row
operations.meaning: Update or delete the row the cursor is on.

operations.name: rows_affected
operations.meaning: How many rows the statement just run read or changed. Every statement resets it.

operations.name: last_identity(scope)
operations.meaning: The last identity value generated: in this routine's scope, anywhere in the session, or for a named table by any session.

operations.name: next_sequence_value
operations.meaning: Take the next number from a named sequence. Numbers are never reused, including after a rollback.

operations.name: set_session_option
operations.meaning: Change a setting that alters how later statements behave: language, first day of the week, null comparison, explicit identity values.

operations.name: session_value
operations.meaning: A value belonging to the session or the machine: the login, the host, the database name, the session number, or a named value set earlier.

operations.name: role_membership
operations.meaning: Whether the current user belongs to a role.

operations.name: catalog_lookup
operations.meaning: A fact about a database object looked up by name or number at run time.

operations.name: for_each_row
operations.meaning: Run a block once per row of a query, in the query's order, over a snapshot taken at the start. Raised from the fetch-loop idiom.

operations.name: atomic_region
operations.meaning: A block whose changes all happen or none do. Raised from a begin and commit that enclose it on every path.

operations.name: named_result
operations.meaning: A query's rows under a name, fixed at the point of definition. Raised from a temp table that is filled once and then only read.

operations.name: column_expression_function
operations.meaning: A scalar function with no loop and no data access, restated as a single expression over its parameters.

operations.name: read_table
operations.meaning: All rows of a table, view, temp table or row-set variable, in no particular order.

operations.name: read_changed_rows
operations.meaning: In a trigger, the rows as they are after the statement (inserted) or as they were before it (deleted).

operations.name: read_values
operations.meaning: A row set written out in the code.

operations.name: call_table_function
operations.meaning: The rows a table-valued function returns for given arguments.

operations.name: read_as_of
operations.meaning: A table's rows as they were at a point in time, or over a period, by the table's own period columns.

operations.name: search_text_index
operations.meaning: Rows of a table matching a full-text condition, each with a rank.

operations.name: shred_json
operations.meaning: Turn JSON text into rows.

operations.name: shred_xml
operations.meaning: Turn the nodes of an XML value that match a path into rows.

operations.name: named_query
operations.meaning: A query given a name for use later in the same statement.

operations.name: recursive_named_query
operations.meaning: A named query that refers to itself: an anchor, then a step repeated until it adds no rows or a stated depth is reached.

operations.name: filter
operations.meaning: Keep the rows for which a condition is true. False and unknown both drop the row.

operations.name: project
operations.meaning: Compute named columns from each row.

operations.name: join(kind)
operations.meaning: Pair rows of two inputs that satisfy a condition: inner, left, right, full or cross. A null never equals a null.

operations.name: lateral_join(kind)
operations.meaning: For each row of the left input, evaluate the right input using that row, and pair them. 'outer' keeps left rows with no match.

operations.name: aggregate
operations.meaning: Group rows by key expressions and compute one row per group. With no keys, exactly one row even for empty input. Null keys form one group.

operations.name: aggregate_grouping_sets
operations.meaning: Aggregate at several levels of grouping at once, including subtotals and a grand total.

operations.name: window
operations.meaning: Compute a value for each row from the rows around it, by partition, order and frame, without merging rows.

operations.name: distinct
operations.meaning: Remove duplicate rows. For strings, 'duplicate' follows the column's comparison rule, and which spelling survives is undefined.

operations.name: sort
operations.meaning: Order rows by keys. Nulls come first ascending. Strings order by their comparison rule. Order among equal keys is undefined.

operations.name: limit
operations.meaning: Keep the first n rows or n percent, optionally with every row that ties with the last. Without a sort, which rows is undefined.

operations.name: skip_and_limit
operations.meaning: Skip a number of sorted rows, then keep a number.

operations.name: union(all)
operations.meaning: The rows of both inputs, with or without duplicates removed.

operations.name: intersect
operations.meaning: Rows present in both inputs, duplicates removed. Nulls match nulls here.

operations.name: except
operations.meaning: Rows of the first input not present in the second, duplicates removed. Nulls match nulls here.

operations.name: pivot
operations.meaning: Turn the distinct values of one column into columns, aggregating another.

operations.name: unpivot
operations.meaning: Turn a set of columns into rows of name and value, dropping nulls.

operations.name: to_json
operations.meaning: Format a query's rows as one JSON text.

operations.name: to_xml
operations.meaning: Format a query's rows as one XML value.

operations.name: insert_rows
operations.meaning: Add rows to a table from a query or a list of values. Columns not named take their default or generated value. Constraints and triggers apply.

operations.name: update_rows
operations.meaning: Change columns of the rows of a table that satisfy a condition, optionally taking values from joined rows. If a row matches several joined rows, which one is used is undefined.

operations.name: delete_rows
operations.meaning: Remove the rows of a table that satisfy a condition, optionally chosen by joining other rows or through a named query.

operations.name: merge_rows
operations.meaning: Compare a table with a source on a condition and, per clause, update or delete matched rows, insert unmatched source rows, and update or delete target rows with no source. A target row matched by several source rows is an error for an update.

operations.name: return_changed_rows
operations.meaning: From a write, give back one row per row inserted, updated or deleted, with its values before and after and the action taken, to the caller or into a table.

operations.name: create_table_from_query
operations.meaning: Create a table with a query's columns and fill it with its rows.

operations.name: truncate_table
operations.meaning: Remove every row of a table and reset its identity counter. No trigger fires.

operations.name: bulk_load
operations.meaning: Load rows from a file.

operations.name: literal
operations.meaning: A typed constant.

operations.name: null
operations.meaning: The absent value, with a type.

operations.name: column
operations.meaning: A column of a named input, resolved against the catalog or scope.

operations.name: variable
operations.meaning: The current value of a variable or parameter.

operations.name: scalar_query
operations.meaning: The single value of a query used as an expression: null for no row, an error for more than one.

operations.name: call_scalar_function
operations.meaning: The value of a scalar function for given arguments.

operations.name: updated_column_test
operations.meaning: In a trigger, whether the statement named a column in its list of columns to set, whatever value it set.

operations.name: convert
operations.meaning: Change a value to a type by SQL Server's rules. A value that cannot convert is an error.

operations.name: convert_with_style
operations.meaning: Convert between text and a date, number or binary using a numbered format.

operations.name: try_convert
operations.meaning: As convert, giving null where the value cannot convert.

operations.name: implicit_convert
operations.meaning: A conversion the source did not write, added by lowering wherever SQL Server's type precedence makes one happen.

operations.name: fit_to_type
operations.meaning: Make a value fit a declared type on assignment or storage: cut a string without error, pad a fixed string, round a date and time, truncate money.

operations.name: add
operations.meaning: Sum of two numbers, typed by precedence. Overflow is an error.

operations.name: subtract
operations.meaning: Difference of two numbers. Overflow is an error.

operations.name: multiply
operations.meaning: Product of two numbers. Overflow is an error.

operations.name: integer_divide
operations.meaning: Quotient of two integers, truncated toward zero. Division by zero is an error.

operations.name: decimal_divide
operations.meaning: Quotient of exact decimals, with SQL Server's result precision and scale. Division by zero is an error.

operations.name: money_multiply
operations.meaning: Product involving money, truncated to four places.

operations.name: money_divide
operations.meaning: Quotient involving money, truncated to four places.

operations.name: float_divide
operations.meaning: Quotient of floating-point numbers.

operations.name: modulo
operations.meaning: Remainder, with the sign of the dividend.

operations.name: negate
operations.meaning: The number with its sign changed.

operations.name: round(digits, truncate)
operations.meaning: Round half away from zero to a number of digits, or truncate; the result keeps the input's type.

operations.name: numeric_function(name)
operations.meaning: Absolute value, ceiling, floor, power, square root, sign, logarithms, each typed as SQL Server types it.

operations.name: is_numeric_text
operations.meaning: Whether text would convert to any numeric type by SQL Server's rules, which accept currency signs, a lone plus or minus, and exponents.

operations.name: random_number
operations.meaning: A pseudo-random number. Cannot be reproduced.

operations.name: new_guid
operations.meaning: A new unique identifier. Cannot be reproduced.

operations.name: compare(operator, rule)
operations.meaning: Equal, not equal, less, greater and their combinations, giving true, false or unknown. Unknown whenever either side is null. For strings 'rule' is the collation's comparison rule.

operations.name: compare_null_as_value
operations.meaning: Equality in which null equals null, as written under ANSI_NULLS off.

operations.name: is_null
operations.meaning: Whether a value is null. Never unknown.

operations.name: and
operations.meaning: True if both are true, false if either is false, otherwise unknown.

operations.name: or
operations.meaning: True if either is true, false if both are false, otherwise unknown.

operations.name: not
operations.meaning: True becomes false, false becomes true, unknown stays unknown.

operations.name: between
operations.meaning: Whether a value lies between two bounds, both included.

operations.name: in_list
operations.meaning: Whether a value equals any of a list. Unknown if it equals none and the list contains a null.

operations.name: in_query
operations.meaning: Whether a value equals any value a query returns, with the same null behaviour.

operations.name: exists
operations.meaning: Whether a query returns at least one row. Never unknown.

operations.name: like(rule)
operations.meaning: Whether text matches a pattern with T-SQL's wildcards: percent, underscore, bracketed sets and ranges, and an optional escape character. Follows the comparison rule.

operations.name: case
operations.meaning: The result of the first branch whose condition is true, else the default, else null. Typed by the highest-precedence branch.

operations.name: first_non_null
operations.meaning: The first argument that is not null, typed by the highest-precedence argument.

operations.name: null_replacement
operations.meaning: The first argument unless it is null, then the second, converted to the first argument's type.

operations.name: null_if_equal(rule)
operations.meaning: Null if the two arguments compare equal, else the first.

operations.name: concat_null_propagating
operations.meaning: Join strings; null if any part is null.

operations.name: concat_null_as_empty
operations.meaning: Join values as text, treating null as an empty string.

operations.name: length_without_trailing_spaces
operations.meaning: Number of characters, not counting spaces at the end.

operations.name: byte_length
operations.meaning: Number of bytes a value occupies as stored.

operations.name: upper
operations.meaning: Text in upper case.

operations.name: lower
operations.meaning: Text in lower case.

operations.name: trim(side)
operations.meaning: Text with spaces removed from the left, the right or both.

operations.name: substring
operations.meaning: Part of a string from a position counted from 1 for a length. A start below 1 shortens the result by the shortfall.

operations.name: left_part
operations.meaning: The first n characters.

operations.name: right_part
operations.meaning: The last n characters.

operations.name: position_of(rule)
operations.meaning: Where one string first occurs in another from a starting position, counted from 1; 0 if absent.

operations.name: pattern_position(rule)
operations.meaning: Where a pattern first matches in a string; 0 if nowhere.

operations.name: replace_text(rule)
operations.meaning: Every occurrence of one string replaced by another, matched by the comparison rule.

operations.name: overlay
operations.meaning: Remove a length of characters at a position and insert a string there. Null when the start is below 1 or past the end, or the length is negative.

operations.name: repeat_text
operations.meaning: A string repeated n times.

operations.name: reverse_text
operations.meaning: A string with its characters in reverse order.

operations.name: character_from_code
operations.meaning: The character for a code, in the database's code page or in Unicode.

operations.name: code_of_character
operations.meaning: The code of the first character.

operations.name: quote_identifier
operations.meaning: A name wrapped in delimiters with any delimiter inside it doubled.

operations.name: format_value
operations.meaning: A number or date as text by a format pattern and culture.

operations.name: split_text
operations.meaning: Rows of the pieces of a string between separators.

operations.name: current_time(kind)
operations.meaning: The moment the statement started: local time to 1/300 of a second, local time to 100 nanoseconds, or UTC. The same throughout one statement.

operations.name: date_add(part)
operations.meaning: A date or time moved by a whole number of a unit. Moving by months clamps to the last day of the month.

operations.name: date_diff_boundaries(part)
operations.meaning: How many boundaries of a unit lie between two moments. Not elapsed time: 23:59 to 00:01 is one day.

operations.name: date_part(part)
operations.meaning: One field of a date or time as a number. Week and weekday depend on the session's first day of the week.

operations.name: date_name(part)
operations.meaning: One field of a date as text in the session's language.

operations.name: date_from_parts
operations.meaning: A date or time built from numbers. An impossible date is an error.

operations.name: end_of_month
operations.meaning: The last day of a date's month.

operations.name: is_date_text
operations.meaning: Whether text would convert to a date and time under the session's language and date format.

operations.name: change_offset
operations.meaning: A date and time moved to, or labelled with, an offset from UTC or a named time zone.

operations.name: count_rows
operations.meaning: Number of rows, as a 32-bit integer; overflow is an error.

operations.name: count_values
operations.meaning: Number of non-null values of an expression, optionally distinct by its comparison rule.

operations.name: sum
operations.meaning: Total of non-null values, typed as SQL Server types it: an integer total stays a 32-bit integer and overflows as an error. Null for no values.

operations.name: average
operations.meaning: Total of non-null values divided by their count, typed as SQL Server types it: over integers the result is an integer, truncated. Null for no values.

operations.name: minimum
operations.meaning: Smallest non-null value; for strings by the comparison rule.

operations.name: maximum
operations.meaning: Largest non-null value; for strings by the comparison rule.

operations.name: join_text
operations.meaning: Non-null values joined with a separator, in a stated order.

operations.name: statistical_aggregate(name)
operations.meaning: Standard deviation or variance, sample or population.

operations.name: row_number
operations.meaning: 1, 2, 3 within a partition in a stated order. Order among ties is undefined.

operations.name: rank(dense)
operations.meaning: Position within a partition, ties sharing a position, with or without gaps after them.

operations.name: bucket_number
operations.meaning: Which of n nearly equal groups a row falls in.

operations.name: offset_value(direction)
operations.meaning: A value from a row a number of positions before or after the current one.

operations.name: frame_value(end)
operations.meaning: The first or last value in the window frame.

operations.name: hash_bytes(algorithm, encoding)
operations.meaning: A hash of a value's bytes. 'encoding' states how text became bytes, which differs between single-byte and UTF-16 strings.

operations.name: compress_bytes(direction)
operations.meaning: GZip compression or decompression.

operations.name: json_value(kind)
operations.meaning: A scalar or a fragment taken from JSON text by a path, a modified copy of the text, or whether text is valid JSON.

operations.name: xml_value(kind)
operations.meaning: A scalar or a fragment taken from an XML value by a path expression, or whether a path matches.

syntax_only.about: Words the corpus scan finds before a parenthesis that are syntax, not operations. Listed so the check knows they were considered.

aliases_seen.about: Names in the corpus that look like function calls and are table aliases with a column list, all from XML shredding in AdventureWorks views.
